title: Chapter 210: Rest Stop
html:
About half an hour later, Captain Yan’s team arrived. They had been assigned to the Third Sick Hall case.

“You’re Chen Ge?” Their leader was a broad-shouldered young man.

“Yes.” Chen Ge had never seen him at the local station; he was probably no ordinary patrol officer.

“Come with us. Until the victim regains consciousness, we’re responsible for your safety.” The words were courteous, though his tone was not. Inspector Lee gave Chen Ge a discreet signal, reassuring him enough to accompany the group to the hospital.

At 11:30 p.m., Gu Feiyu awoke and told the police what had happened. Though barely conscious when Chen Ge attacked the woman, he remembered seeing his rescuer.

He had believed he was about to die, and the experience would haunt him for life. At his insistence, the police arranged a meeting with Chen Ge. Gu Feiyu’s manner was entirely different from their first encounter. A straightforward young man, he clasped Chen Ge’s hand and thanked him with complete sincerity.

The police’s suspicions gradually dissolved. Their young leader praised Chen Ge until he grew embarrassed. Around midnight, Chen Ge left the hospital and stood at an empty intersection, gazing across the darkened city.

“I should tell them.” Holding the torn flyer, he called Captain Yan.

“Xiao Chen?”

“Captain Yan, I have something to tell you.”

“Is this about Patient No. 2? Don’t worry. I’ve received the report. You saved a life—well done.” Captain Yan’s tone hardened. “But I still disapprove of your private investigations. You’re gambling with your life.”

“Don’t worry. Finding Patient No. 2 was a complete coincidence. It won’t happen again.” Chen Ge’s voice was hoarse. “I called for another reason. While listening to her, I heard her mention an unusual organization called the Ghost Stories Society.”

“Ghost story society?”

“The name makes it sound like a club for horror enthusiasts, but they don’t tell fiction—only stories that actually happened.”

“When did you hear this? Who was Patient No. 2 speaking to? Could the conversation be recorded on her phone?” Suspicion entered Captain Yan’s voice.

“She wasn’t on the phone. She had an older-sister persona, so she often spoke to herself.” Chen Ge kept the torn flyer to himself. “I suspect the escaped Third Sick Hall patients formed the society, and that she belonged to it.”

“A ghost-story society founded by escaped psychiatric patients?” After considering it, Captain Yan said gravely, “I’ll have my people investigate. If you learn anything else, call me.”

“Of course.”

After hanging up, Chen Ge raised his collar against the night. They must share a true story every week. What happens when they have none—do they create one?

Chen Ge returned to New Century Park. As he entered the Haunted House, the white cat descended from its tree and followed with elegant indifference. “Next time, I’m tying you up and taking you with me!”

After feeding the cat, Chen Ge checked the black phone’s refreshed Daily Missions. Two were familiar: eliminate hidden safety hazards and hire a new employee. The third was new. It required him to build a rest area outside the Haunted House within one day; the difficulty was Normal.

The black phone’s missions reflect what the Haunted House needs most. With visitor numbers rising, making people stand in line for hours is unsustainable.

He accepted the mission and began sketching a simple rest area.

The budget is too small. With enough money, I could build a multipurpose facility beside the Haunted House—a place to rest, buy food and drinks, and purchase merchandise.

Ideas flooded in. I could borrow from Tian Teng Medical School and install a large screen introducing each scenario. Selected visitor footage could play between introductions, stirring everyone else’s curiosity.

He kept drawing. For each difficulty level, he designed leaderboards ranked by completion time—perfect bait for thrill-seekers and competitive visitors. By the time he finished, the proposal filled several pages.

Chen Ge organized the pages to show Director Luo the next morning, hoping to win his support. A glance at the clock revealed it was already 2 a.m. He stretched.

The only hidden danger left is that door, but it appears only at midnight and cannot affect visitors. The black phone’s repeated warnings must mean I should deal with it anyway. Hiring someone is easier—I can recruit from Tian Teng Medical School. But it isn’t time to make that move yet.

Tapping his pen against the table, Chen Ge compared the two attractions. Pride did not blind him; he understood exactly where his Haunted House lagged behind Tian Teng Medical School.

Tian Teng Medical School is small, but its scenes flow seamlessly together. My Haunted House is larger, yet much of that space feels empty.

That was hardly his fault. He had owned the black phone for barely a week and spent most of that time completing missions and expanding the attraction. Flaws were inevitable.

I should add more scares in my Haunted House. Looks like I need to go make a new batch of props and mannequins tomorrow.

Several Trial Missions had taught Chen Ge countless new ways to frighten people. Ideas crowded his mind, and he smiled as he imagined the resulting screams.

I can’t wait. I wonder who will be so lucky to be the first visitor to visit the Third Sick Hall.

White fur flashed before his eyes. Apparently annoyed by the noise, the cat leaped onto the table, then the bed, and burrowed into the mattress.

Realizing how late it was, Chen Ge set an alarm for 7 a.m. and lay down beside the cat.

At sunrise, Chen Ge cleaned the Haunted House and left with the proposal he had drafted the night before.
